column2: Pass the slot to a sergeant
He graduated. He'll remember your gesture.
You're planning a company morale event. Budget: $0. Expectations: high. What do you do?
Organize a chili cook-off
Fifteen chilis. One hospitalization. Great success.
Mandatory fun run
Nothing says morale like running at 0530.
Relieved of Command?
A soldier in your company was killed in a training accident. The investigation is examining your safety procedures. How do you handle it?
You were cleared. You still think about it every day.
Relieved for loss of confidence. Your career is likely over.
Lawyer up
Cleared. But people noticed you got defensive.
Port Visit Brief
You're liberty officer for a port visit to {country}. 400 sailors. You must keep them out of jail. Strategy?
Strict buddy rule
Zero incidents. A miracle at sea.
Trust the crew
Only two minor incidents.
A sailor tried to steal a horse. International incident.
Captain's Career Course
You're at the career course. Your study group wants to copy last year's answers. What do you do?
Do your own work
You learned and graduated honestly.
Copy along
The instructor noticed. Honor code violation.
It's September. Your battalion must spend $2 million in two weeks or lose it next year. What do you buy?
New gym equipment
The soldiers love it. Morale up.
Office furniture
Ergonomic chairs for everyone. Thrilling.
Return the money
Fiscally honorable. The brigade commander thinks you're crazy.
A member of Congress is touring your installation tomorrow. The barracks have mold and broken AC. What do you show them?
Show them the real barracks
Funding approved for renovation within a year.
The general is furious you embarrassed the command.
Tour went well. Nothing changed.
A national reporter asks you about a recent training accident on camera. Public affairs is sweating. What do you say?
Be candid and compassionate
Clip went viral for the right reasons.
One sentence was taken out of context.
No comment
Headline: "Commander Dodges Questions."
General's Pet Project
The two-star wants your brigade to pilot a new "Wellness Initiative" with 47 mandatory briefings. Your soldiers are drowning in requirements. What do you do?
Salute and execute
The general is pleased. Your troops are not.
Push back with data
The general trimmed it to 10 briefings. You're a hero.
The general called you "not a team player." Ouch.
Brigade Command Selection
The centralized selection list is out. Your name is on it as an alternate. What do you do?
Wait patiently
A principal declined. You're in command.
No slot opened. Next year.
Call your mentors
Someone made a call. You're in.
Looked desperate. Nothing changed.
Toxic Leader Complaint
A command climate survey shows one of your battalion commanders is toxic. He's also your best tactician. What do you do?
Relieve him
Hard call. The battalion's climate improved fast.
Counsel him
He changed his ways. Somewhat.
A soldier's suicide note named him. Now it's on you.
A major hurricane hit the coast. You've been put in charge of joint relief operations. Roads are flooded and communications are down. Priorities?
Air rescue first
Your helicopters pulled 300 people off rooftops.
Restore communications
Once comms came up, everything got faster.
Wait for higher guidance
Precious hours lost. Criticism in the news.
You have 26 years in. A defense contractor offers you triple your salary to retire and consult. What do you do?
Retire and cash in
Retired with honors. Now you sell drones to your old friends.
Stay in for stars
You're going for general. Family sighs.
A foreign general from {country} is visiting and serves you a local delicacy: fermented sheep eye. Everyone watches. What do you do?
Eat it with a smile
Diplomatic success. Your stomach disagrees.
Awkward. The partnership stalled for a week.
Classified Briefing Leak
Your staff's classified briefing just appeared on a gaming chat server. The press is calling. What's your move?
Launch an investigation
It was a junior analyst trying to win an argument. Contained.
Downplay it
It blew over.
Congress demanded answers. Your career took a hit.
You've been assigned to the Pentagon. Long hours, no troops, endless staff work. How do you approach it?
Network hard
You met all the right people. Stars may be in your future.
Count the days
You survived. Barely.
Your installation has lost four soldiers to suicide in two months. What do you do?
Overhaul mental health access
Embedded counselors, no-stigma policies. Numbers improved.
Mandatory briefing
Another PowerPoint. Nothing changed.
General Officer Board
Your file is in front of the general officer selection board. One black mark from a decade ago. What do you do?
Hope your record speaks
Selected for general. Stars!
Not selected. Your career may have peaked.
Write a letter to the board
Your explanation landed. Selected.
It drew more attention to the issue.
IED on the Route
Your convoy is rolling through {country} when the lead vehicle stops. Something looks off in the road ahead. What do you do?
EOD found a pressure plate IED. Patience saved lives.
Drive around it
You made it around.
killed by an IED
A secondary device detonated under your vehicle.
The base sirens wail: "INCOMING!" You're in the shower, naked and soapy. What do you do?
Sprint to the bunker
You made it in a towel. Everyone has seen everything now.
Hit the deck where you are
Rounds landed 200 meters away. Back to the shower.
Shrapnel punched through the shower trailer.
Your patrol in {country} gets ambushed. Rounds are cracking overhead and {buddy} is down in the open. What do you do?
Drag {buddy} to cover
You pulled {buddy} behind a wall under fire. Bronze Star.
killed rescuing a buddy under fire
You were hit getting to {buddy}.
Your fire suppressed them. A medic got to {buddy}.
A round hit your arm.
You couldn't move. Someone else saved {buddy}. You can't forgive yourself.
Grenade in the Room
A grenade bounces into the room where your squad is taking cover. There's no time. What do you do?
Jump on it
Your body armor absorbed most of it. You survived. Medal of Honor.
killed smothering a grenade to save the squad
You saved everyone in that room.
Kick it out
It exploded outside. Everyone lived.
It went off at the doorway.
Dive for cover
Everyone dove. Minor injuries.
Fragments in your legs.
A single shot cracks past your head on an observation post. A sniper is somewhere in the buildings. What do you do?
Get down and report
Air support handled the building. You're shaken but alive.
Try to spot him
You spotted the glint. Called it in. Threat eliminated.
killed by a sniper
He saw you first.
A soldier is bleeding out on a dusty field. The medevac is 30 minutes away. You're the closest one with a tourniquet. What do you do?
Apply the tourniquet
You stopped the bleed. He made it to surgery.
You did everything right. He didn't make it.
The medic got there. It was close.
Since returning from {country}, you wake up drenched in sweat, hearing explosions. Fireworks make you hit the ground. What do you do?
Go to behavioral health
Therapy is hard but helping.
Drink to sleep
It works until it doesn't.
{buddy} has the same dreams. You're not alone.
Your back, knees, and hearing are shot. The VA claim process is 80 pages long. What do you do?
Get a VSO to help
A Veterans Service Officer got you a fair rating.
Do it yourself
Approved. You're a bureaucratic warrior.
Denied. Appeal pending. Forever.
Other people need it more. Your knees disagree.
After nine months in {country}, your plane lands. Your family is in the gym waiting with signs. How do you feel?
Run to them
Hugs, tears, and your dog lost its mind.
Hang back, overwhelmed
It's a lot. Readjusting will take time.
You got orders to a new duty station across the country. The movers broke your TV and lost a box. What do you do?
File a claim
Reimbursed in only four months!
Claim denied. "Pre-existing damage."
Do a DITY move next time
You moved yourself and pocketed the difference.
Between deployments and field time, you've been home 90 days this year. Your spouse says they're exhausted. What do you do?
Marriage retreat
The chaplain-run retreat helped more than you expected.
They moved back to their parents' place.
Talk honestly
A long, hard conversation. You're okay.
It turned into a fight.
Your unit is deployed to help after a massive earthquake in {country}. A child is trapped under rubble. What do you do?
Dig with your hands
You pulled her out alive. Her mother kissed your hands.
An aftershock collapsed more rubble. You were too late.
Wait for heavy equipment
The crane arrived. She survived, barely.
You're eligible for the GI Bill. College, trade school, or transfer it to your kid?
Go to college
Tuition paid plus a housing stipend.
Trade school
Welding certification. Solid.
Transfer to your child
Your kid will go to college debt-free.
Mail From Home
You get a care package from an elementary school class. Crayon drawings and beef jerky. What do you do?
Write them back
They framed your letter in the classroom.
Share the jerky
Your squad loved it.
Your ears have been ringing for a week after a live-fire exercise without proper protection. What do you do?
Get it checked
Mild damage documented. Good for future VA claims.
What? You say that a lot now.
Rockets are hitting the base in {country}. You're crossing open ground near the motor pool. What do you do?
Dive into a ditch
Dirt in your teeth, but alive.
Shrapnel caught your shoulder.
Run for the bunker
Made it in time.
killed in a rocket attack
A rocket landed close.
{buddy} was killed by a roadside bomb this morning. The memorial is tomorrow. How do you deal with it?
Speak at the memorial
You told the funny stories. Everyone laughed and cried.
Bottle it up
You haven't cried. You haven't slept either.
Visit the chaplain
It didn't fix anything. But it helped.
A stray cat has adopted your outpost in {country}. General Order No. 1 prohibits pets. Keep it?
Sergeant Whiskers keeps the rats away. Morale soars.
The command sergeant major found Whiskers.
Ship it home
Through a nonprofit, Whiskers now lives with your family.
You've been assigned to burn pit duty. The black smoke smells like plastic and death. No respirator available. What do you do?
Do the job
You coughed for a month. Hope it doesn't catch up later.
Complain to medical
They found you a mask.
No masks in stock.
Coast Guard Drug Bust
Your cutter intercepts a semi-submersible full of cocaine. The smugglers are scrambling to scuttle it. What do you do?
Board immediately
4,000 pounds seized. Headlines back home.
It sank fast. You barely got off it.
Rescue the crew first
Crew detained. Most of the drugs sank, but nobody died.
You're monitoring satellite feeds and see a convoy forming near friendly troops. It might be civilians. What do you report?
Report what you see, no guess
Command got more eyes on it. Civilians. A bad call avoided.
Flag it as hostile
It was a wedding party. You think about it constantly.
Base Housing Lottery
Base housing has a waiting list of six months. A friend says he knows "a guy" who can bump you up for $500. What do you do?
Pay the guy
Keys in a week.
The guy was a scammer. And you're now in an investigation.
Six months in a budget hotel. You hate it.
Typhoon at Sea
A typhoon is battering the ship. Waves are crashing over the bow and something is loose on deck. What do you do?
Secure it
Tethered and secured. Chief nodded at you.
swept overboard in a typhoon
A wave slammed you into a bulkhead.
It broke loose and smashed a radar mast.
Interpreter's Plea
The interpreter who saved your life in {country} is now being hunted. He emails you for a visa recommendation. What do you do?
Write the letter
He got a visa. You picked him up from the airport.
Ignore the email
You never heard from him again.
Drunk Brawl Overseas
In a bar in {country}, a local starts a fight with {buddy}. The local police are already nearby. What do you do?
You dragged {buddy} out the back door. International incident avoided.
Join the fight
You won and fled. Legends.
Arrested. The embassy got involved.
Wrong Way Bombing Range
During a live-fire exercise, you notice a vehicle has wandered onto the bombing range. Jets are inbound. What do you do?
Call "Knock it off!"
Strike aborted. A lost farmer. You saved his life.
Assume someone else sees it
Someone else called it.
Tragedy. You will relive it forever.
Your back injury is getting worse. The doctor recommends a medical board, which could end your career. What do you do?
Accept the board
Medically retired. A new chapter.
Hide the pain
You're still in. But at what cost?
A massive wildfire is threatening a town near base. The governor requests military help. You volunteer. What do you do?
Dig firebreaks
Exhausting work. The town was saved.
Help evacuate residents
You carried an elderly man to safety. He cried.
Chow Hall Mystery Meat
The dining facility is serving something labeled "Meat." Just "Meat." You're starving. Eat it?
Surprisingly decent. You still don't know what it was.
Food poisoning. Two days on the toilet.
Go for the salad bar
Iceberg lettuce and ranch. Living the dream.
Night watch in an old building on base. You hear footsteps on the floor above. It's supposed to be empty. What do you do?
It was a raccoon. You screamed louder than it did.
Nothing there. But the door you locked is now open.
Turn up the radio
You didn't sleep for days.
You find out someone has been recording people in the shower trailers. You know who it is. What do you do?
Report to CID
He was arrested and court-martialed.
He broke down and confessed.
He attacked you and destroyed the evidence.
A stranger at a restaurant thanks you for your service and wants to pay for your meal. What do you do?
Accept graciously
Nice gesture. You tipped the waitress extra.
Awkward smiles all around.
A fellow service member is posting heated political rants in uniform on social media. What do you do?
Remind them of the rules
They deleted it. Barely.
Join the argument
Now you're both in trouble.
Your unit lost radio contact with higher in {country}. You're the only one who knows the backup satellite system. What do you do?
Set it up under pressure
Comms restored in four minutes. They called you a wizard.
The battery was dead. Nobody charged it.
Send a runner
Old school, but it worked.
You need new boots. The issue ones gave you blisters. The PX sells $250 boots that are actually comfortable. Buy?
Buy the good boots
Your feet thank you every single day.
Blisters forever.
Your hometown newspaper wants to do a story about your service. Your old high school bully reads it. What do you say in the interview?
Classy article. Your mom framed it.
Exaggerate a bit
You might have implied you were a Navy SEAL. You were not.
Day 4 of SFAS. Your heels look like raw hamburger and the next ruck is 12 miles with 55 lbs. What will you do?
Tape up and push
You finish inside the time standard. The cadre write something down. You choose to believe it was good.
You hobble in late. The cadre write something down. It was not good.
The medic drains them and shrugs. 'Your call, candidate.' You lose a little time but keep your feet.
You sign the voluntary withdrawal form. The ride back is very quiet.
The Star Course
Solo land navigation at Camp Mackall, night, no lights. Your points are across a swamp nobody wants to cross. What will you do?
Cut straight through
Waist-deep and miserable, but you hit every point with time to spare.
You lose your pace count in the muck and wander until sunrise.
Take the long way
Slow but solid. You hit your points with minutes left.
You're too slow and miss one point.
Walk on the road
Nobody sees you. You feel guilty and fast.
A cadre truck is parked right there, lights off. Road walking is an instant problem.
Team Week. Six candidates, one telephone pole, and a cadre who says the log 'looks lonely.' {buddy} is visibly slacking. What will you do?
Carry extra weight
Your shoulders scream, but the peers notice who carried the load.
{buddy} picks it up. Nobody likes you, but the log moves.
Arguing under a log goes badly. The cadre love it. You don't.
Coast too
Nobody notices. This time.
Peer evals are brutal. Everyone noticed.
Cadre hand you a sheet: rank your team from best to worst. {buddy} has carried you all week but has a big ego. What will you do?
Rank honestly
You rate {buddy} near the top. Honesty is what they're actually grading.
Tank {buddy} to rise
It works. You feel gross about it.
Everyone else rated {buddy} first. The cadre notice the outlier: you.
The Nasty Nick obstacle course. The rope over the water is slick and your grip is gone. What will you do?
Grit through it
You hang on by pure spite and make it across.
Splash. The cadre call you 'Aquaman' for a week.
Use proper technique
Leg lock, slow and steady. Boring and effective.
Technique isn't enough with noodle arms. You fall.
Ride of Shame
Rucking alone at 0300, a cadre truck stops. 'Rough night? Hop in, warm cab, hot coffee.' What will you do?
You say 'No thanks, sergeant' and keep moving. The truck pulls off. That was the test.
Get in the truck
The coffee is great. Your SFAS career is over.
Final formation at SFAS. They read names for 'selected.' Yours is called. {buddy}'s isn't. What will you do?
You tell {buddy} to come back next year. {buddy} swears they will.
Celebrate loudly
You whoop in the formation. Half the room glares.
SERE resistance lab. An 'interrogator' slaps the table and demands your unit's mission. You're cold, hungry, and very tired. What will you do?
Stick to the Code
Name, rank, service number. The instructors debrief you as a solid resister.
You crack and give a believable cover story with real details. The debrief is awkward.
Mouth off
Your sarcasm somehow works on their nerves. Barely.
Mouthing off earns you a lot more stress positions.
The Army assigned you a language for the Q Course. The instructor talks fast and your test is Friday. What will you do?
Flashcards nightly
You pass with a solid score. You start dreaming in verb conjugations.
You study hard and still fail the oral. Recycle.
Practice with natives
You make friends at a local restaurant and your speaking takes off.
You mostly learn slang you can't use on the test.
Somehow you pass. Nobody knows how.
You fail. The team sergeant's face says it all.
18B training: strip and reassemble a foreign machine gun blindfolded, against the clock. What will you do?
Go for speed
You beat the class record. Instructors start calling you 'Hands.'
A spring launches into the dark. You find it after time expires.
Slow and smooth
Clean pass. Slow is smooth, smooth is fast.
Smooth but too slow.
18C class. You must calculate a cutting charge for a steel beam. Your numbers look off. What will you do?
Re-work the formula
You find your decimal error. The beam drops perfectly.
Still wrong. The instructor sighs and shows you.
Add P for plenty
Huge boom. The beam is gone. So is a nearby port-a-john.
Shrapnel dents a range truck. Safety violation. Article 15.
Medic Trauma Lane
18D trauma lane: a screaming simulated casualty, arterial bleed, airway compromised, 3 minutes. What will you do?
Bleed controlled, airway secured. Your instructor nods once, which is huge.
You tighten it too slowly. 'Your patient bled out.'
Airway first
You get lucky. The instructor lectures you on MARCH anyway.
Wrong order. The patient 'dies.' You hear about it all week.
18E commo training. Morse at 13 words per minute. Everything sounds like a cricket being angry. What will you do?
You start hearing words in the beeps. You pass.
Your brain melts and you fail the timed test.
Use a mnemonic app
Weird rhymes stick in your head. Good enough.
The mnemonics collapse under pressure.
Robin Sage Farmer
Robin Sage, North Carolina. A real local farmer playing a 'G-chief' supporter offers his barn and a pot roast. What will you do?
Accept and thank him
Best meal in weeks. You build rapport, which is the whole point.
Stay in the woods
Tactically sound, emotionally devastating. The pot roast haunts you.
Robin Sage. The role-player guerrilla chief demands your team give his fighters your rifles before he'll cooperate. What will you do?
You trade training for trust. The cadre grade you well on rapport.
He storms off. Your detachment loses a day.
He respects the spine. Barely.
He 'kicks you out of Pineland.' Not great.
Static Line Refusal
Airborne School, first jump. The door opens and the ground looks very far away. What will you do?
Go on the green light
Your chute opens. You yell something embarrassing. You're hooked.
Bad landing. You roll your ankle hard.
A jumpmaster gently but firmly removes you from the door and your training.
Military Free Fall school in Yuma. Your first jump from altitude. You go unstable and start spinning. What will you do?
Arch and fight it
You recover, hit your altitude, and pull clean. Instructors give a thumbs up.
You pull while spinning and get a line twist. Hard landing, sore back.
Pull early
Safe, but you get chewed out for pulling high.
Your canopy opens into a mess of lines. You cut away and land on your reserve, shaken.
Combat Diver qualification. Instructors rip your mask and tie your hoses in knots underwater. Lungs burning. What will you do?
Fix it calmly
You untangle every knot and keep your regulator. You pass the pool comp.
Signal out
You live to try again someday. Not this class.
A cadre inspects rucks and finds three candy bars in yours. On a fasting day. What will you do?
'Mine, sergeant.' You do pushups until the candy is a distant memory.
Say it's {buddy}'s
The cadre believe you. {buddy} doesn't speak to you.
{buddy} has an alibi. You are now known as the snack snitch.
Offer to share
The cadre actually laughs. Takes one. Moves on.
He doesn't laugh.
Asleep on Fire Watch
Barracks fire watch at 0300 after three days of no sleep. Your eyes are closing on their own. What will you do?
Pace and drink water
You make it through the shift without incident.
Sit down 'for a second'
You wake up seconds before the next guy shows. Close one.
The staff duty NCO finds you snoring. Article 15.
You see a candidate take {buddy}'s night vision cover. Gear is getting 'borrowed' everywhere. What will you do?
The gear is returned. {buddy} owes you.
Steal one back
{buddy} is squared away. Nobody asks questions.
Now you're the thief on camera. Article 15.
Saturday on Bragg Blvd. A drunk guy calls your beret 'a costume.' {buddy} is already rolling up sleeves. What will you do?
You drag {buddy} out. Your team sergeant would be proud, if bored.
Throw hands
Short fight. Cops arrive late. Nobody presses charges.
Military police, a black eye, and an Article 15.
0630 PT formation and you're still a little drunk from last night. The team sergeant is walking the line. What will you do?
Push through PT
You sweat out the tequila and survive the run.
You throw up during the run. In front of the colonel.
Call in sick
Sick call buys you a day. Nobody pushes.
Sick call doc writes 'alcohol' on the form. Oops.
Just finished the Q Course. A Fayetteville dealer offers you a muscle car at 24% APR, 'military discount.' What will you do?
It's loud, fast, and will cost you more than a house.
Buy a used truck
Boring. Smart. Your team sergeant approves.
The salesman yells 'thank you for your service' at your back.
You got your Long Tab. {buddy} wants matching tattoos of the SF crest tonight. What will you do?
Looks great. Your mom will hate it.
{buddy} gets it alone and calls you a coward for weeks.
New Guy Chores
First week on your ODA. The team sergeant says the team room is 'disgusting' and looks right at you. What will you do?
Clean it spotless
You scrub until it sparkles. The team grunts approval.
Ask 'why me?'
He laughs and assigns it to someone else. Lucky.
Wrong question. Now you clean the cage too.
{buddy} sends you to the supply cage to get a 'box of grid squares' for the land nav class. What will you do?
Go ask for it
The supply sergeant laughs for five full minutes. You're officially initiated.
Call the bluff
'Nice try.' {buddy} grins. You pass the vibe check.
First Partner Range
First deployment to {country}. A partner soldier shoots with his eyes closed and holds the rifle sideways. What will you do?
Patient coaching
By day's end, he's hitting the target. He brings you tea.
He nods, then keeps shooting sideways.
Yell at him
He stops showing up to training. Rapport: zero.
Chai With Elders
In {country}, village elders pour you endless sweet tea. You're full and need to pee badly. What will you do?
Keep drinking
The elders are delighted. Your bladder is not.
No offense taken.
An elder looks insulted. The vibe chills.
Lost at Mackall
Training exercise at Camp Mackall. Your GPS died and the map is soaked. What will you do?
Terrain association
Hills and creeks get you home. Old school wins.
You wander into a different training lane. Embarrassing.
Radio for help
They find you. They also tell everyone.
Halfway through a Q Course field problem, your ankle rolls and pops loudly. What will you do?
Hide it and keep going
You finish. Doc says it's sprained, not broken. Lucky.
It was broken. Now you're recycled for months.
X-ray, crutches, recycle. Painful but smart.
Q Course Graduation
Q Course graduation. Your family flew in. You put on the green beret for the first time. What will you do?
Thank your family
Your dad tries not to cry and fails.
Celebrate with team
Big night out. Little memory of it.
SUT Ambush Lane
Small Unit Tactics lane. You're squad leader and the 'enemy' is coming down the trail early. What will you do?
Initiate the ambush
Clean kill zone. The evaluator gives you a GO.
Half the squad isn't in position. NO-GO.
Let them pass
You wait for the main body. Smart call.
There was no main body. NO-GO.
Squared Away Award
Your training cycle ends. The cadre want to recommend someone as honor graduate. You're in the running. What will you do?
Grind the final week
You earn honor grad and a commendation.
Close, but {buddy} edges you out.
Help others pass
You don't win, but three guys pass because of you.
In {country}, the partner force commander is collecting pay for 40 'soldiers' who don't exist. What will you do?
Report up the chain
An investigation fixes the roster. The commander sulks but complies.
Nothing happens. The commander now hates you.
Confront him directly
He admits it, fixes it, and respects you more.
He stops cooperating with your team.
The fighters you train go unpaid. Some quit.
A new partner recruit in {country} keeps staring at your team and asked when you all sleep. What will you do?
Flag him to intel
He's linked to insurgents. Your vigilance saves lives.
He's just weird. Partner leaders are offended.
Double guard quietly
Exhausting but safe. He deserts a week later.
Nothing happens. You got lucky.
killed in an insider attack
He opens fire inside the wire.
Your 18D skills are needed. A woman in a {country} village is in a hard labor and the nearest hospital is 6 hours away. What will you do?
Deliver the baby
Mother and baby survive. The village names the baby after the team.
Complications you couldn't fix. You'll carry this one.
Call medevac
A helicopter takes her to a hospital in time.
Medevac is refused for a non-combat case.
Free clinic day in {country}. 400 people showed up and you have supplies for 150. What will you do?
Triage hard
You treat the sickest first. Hard choices, best outcome.
First come first served
Fights break out in line. The village elder is not pleased.
An 18C task: the village in {country} needs a well. A local contractor wants twice the going rate. What will you do?
Build it yourselves
Your team digs it. Water flows. Kids cheer.
You hit rock. Project stalls for weeks.
Pay the contractor
The well gets built. Slow and expensive but done.
Your 18E gear dies mid-mission in {country}. Satellite link down, HF static, team needs contact. What will you do?
Rig a field antenna
A wire, a tree, and math. You get through.
Static only. The team goes without comms overnight.
Push to the rally point
You walk out of the dead zone and reestablish.
Afghanistan. Your patrol takes PKM fire from the ridge. Partner forces scatter. {buddy} is pinned in the open. What will you do?
You drag {buddy} behind a wall under fire. Later, a Silver Star.
killed in a valley ambush
You're hit before you get there.
Suppress the ridge
Your machine gun keeps their heads down. {buddy} crawls to cover.
A round finds you behind cover.
Call for fires
Mortars walk onto the ridge. Silence.
Too slow. {buddy} takes a round in the leg.
Syria. ISIS fighters hit your partner force's checkpoint at night. The partners are falling back. What will you do?
You lead from the front. The checkpoint holds. Bronze Star with V.
killed fighting ISIS in Syria
An RPG blast drops you.
Air support
An AC-130 changes the conversation entirely.
Air is retasked. You withdraw.
Niger. Your vehicles are ambushed near a village by 50+ fighters. Comms are spotty. What will you do?
You bound back under fire. Everyone gets out.
killed in an ambush in the Sahel
Vehicles get separated.
Hold and fight
French jets arrive at the last minute. You earned a Silver Star.
killed holding position in Niger
The perimeter collapses.
{buddy} is showing up hungover and shaky. The team sergeant hasn't noticed yet. What will you do?
{buddy} admits it and goes to treatment. You saved a career.
